SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-18: FHIRPath — §6.6 Math Operations, §6.7 Date/Time Arithmetic. Test these items: * (multiplication), / (division), + (addition), - (subtraction), div (truncated division), mod (modulo), & (string concatenation), + (dateTime addition), - (dateTime subtraction). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 §22.1 Integer (-2^31..2^31-1); dual-engine lockstep rule
issues.evidence: Unsuffixed integer literal > INT32_MAX (`2147483648`, `4503599627370497`): Python core returns the value; native C++ throws 'Integer literal out of range' -> empty at UDF; Python-fallback DuckDB also empty. Divergence core vs both DuckDB paths. Long literals (`...L`) are the sanctioned 64-bit form.
issues.root_cause: fhir4ds/fhirpath/engine/evaluators/__init__.py:number_literal accepts any digit string as int; native evaluator.cpp IntegerLiteral enforces INT32 range.
issues.resolution: evaluators/__init__.py number_literal now raises FHIRPathError for unsuffixed Integer literals outside [-2^31, 2^31-1] and Long literals outside int64 (lockstep with native evaluator + N1 §22.1). DuckDB paths already empty.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.6.5 div / §6.6.6 mod — exact truncated division; §4.1.3/§4.1.4 exact Integer/Decimal
issues.evidence: div/mod computed via binary64 on all engines. `9223372036854775807L div 1` -> PY/FB 9223372036854775808 (correct ...807); `9223372036854775806L div 2` -> PY/FB 4611686018427387904 (correct ...903); `2305843009213693951L mod 7` -> NAT 2 (correct 1). Python: int(x/y) float path in math.intdiv; native: std::trunc(l_num/r_num) double path.
issues.resolution: math.py intdiv/mod use exact integer truncated division (_truncated_divmod_int) and Decimal // (exact truncation); native evaluator.cpp adds exact int64 div/mod path for Integer-typed operands (incl. Long). 64-bit operands now exact on all three engines.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §5.5.8 Decimal/Integer toString forbids scientific notation; §6.6.5 div returns Integer
issues.root_cause: Native div routes through double and returns FromDecimal with normalized source_text instead of Integer path.
issues.resolution: Native exact int64 div path returns FPValue::FromInteger — no scientific-notation rendering; value exact.

issues.evidence: `0.10000000000000000000000000001 mod 0.1` (28-digit legal Decimal): native returns 0.0 (binary64 fmod precision loss); PY/FB return exact 1e-29.
issues.root_cause: Native mod uses std::fmod on doubles; no decimal-text exact path.
issues.resolution: Native mod: tryDecimalModExactText (__int128 decimal-text truncated mod with exact source_text) before binary64 fmod; falls back to fmod only on overflow-bail. Matches Python Decimal exactly (0.00000000000000000000000000001).

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.6/§6.7 'evaluation will end and signal an error'; strict-core FHIRPathError contract
issues.evidence: Python core leaks raw TypeError for `1 'cm' div 2` / `1 'cm' mod 2` / `2 div 1 'cm'` (Quantity operands; spec: Integer/Decimal only) and raw ValueError for `@2012-01-01 + 25 hours` / `@2012-01-01 + 1 'a'` (invalid unit per §6.7.1). DuckDB wrappers already convert to empty.
issues.root_cause: math.intdiv/mod let Quantity operands fall into float()/int() coercion; datetime plus raises ValueError.
issues.resolution: math.py intdiv/mod raise FHIRPathError for Quantity operands; _temporal_plus wrapper converts ValueError from FP_TimeBase.plus (invalid §6.7.1 unit) to FHIRPathError.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.6.2 division always Decimal; dual-engine lockstep doctrine
issues.evidence: Pre-existing display divergence: `1 / 3` native renders shortest-round-trip '0.3333333333333333' (16 digits) while Python fallback/core render 28-digit Decimal '0.3333333333333333333333333333'. Numeric values agree (equality passes); only source_text rendering differs. Also PY core renders `2147483647 * 2` as Decimal('4294967294') vs engines '4294967294.0'.
issues.root_cause: Native '/' uses normalizeDecimalMathSourceText (shortest-round-trip) by design (FP-18 HISTORIAN QA-001 comment); fallback uses Python Decimal context (28 sig digits).
issues.resolution: DEFERRED: matching native to the fallback requires porting Python decimal-context division (28-sig-digit half-even) to C++; no official fixture pins the rendering; numeric equality already agrees; FP-01-adjacent.
